items.exampleEn: She looked critically at her drawing and started again.
items.exampleZh: 她挑剔地看了看自己的畫，然後重畫一張。

items.exampleEn: His smile was misleading; he was actually very angry.
items.exampleZh: 他的笑容會讓人誤會，其實他非常生氣。

items.exampleEn: My answer and my sister's answer coincided exactly.
items.exampleZh: 我和我姊妹的答案完全一致。

items.exampleEn: Here's a paradox: the more choices a shop offers, the harder it is to choose.
items.exampleZh: 有個矛盾的現象：店裡提供的選擇越多，就越難做決定。

items.exampleEn: Good cooks can discriminate between many kinds of salt.
items.exampleZh: 好廚師分辨得出很多種鹽的差別。

items.exampleEn: His anger was understandable after waiting three hours.
items.exampleZh: 等了三個小時，他會生氣是可以理解的。

items.exampleEn: The team needs a coherent plan for the next year.
items.exampleZh: 這個團隊需要一套前後連貫的明年計畫。

items.exampleEn: There is some ambiguity in the rules of the game.
items.exampleZh: 這個遊戲的規則有些地方不太明確。

items.sentenceEn: Having more free time but feeling busier is a strange paradox.
items.sentenceZh: 空閒時間變多了，卻覺得更忙，這是個奇怪的矛盾。

items.audioEn: The concert coincides with my exam, so I can't go.
items.audioZh: 那場音樂會跟我的考試撞期，所以我不能去。
items.questionZh: 說話者為什麼不能去音樂會？
options: The concert is too far away
It's on the day of a test

items.sentenceEn: The signs at the station were misleading, so we took the wrong train.
items.sentenceZh: 車站的指標會誤導人，所以我們搭錯了車。

items.sentenceEn: It's understandable to feel nervous before your first day at work.
items.sentenceZh: 上班第一天前會緊張，是可以理解的。

items.stemEn: The message had some ____, so we each understood it differently.
items.stemZh: 那則訊息有點模稜兩可，所以我們每個人的理解都不一樣。

items.stemEn: He was so sleepy that what he said was hardly ____.
items.stemZh: 他睏到說出來的話幾乎不成句。

items.passageEn: In our media class last month, we learned to read advertisements critically. Our teacher showed us an ad for a fruit drink with glamorous people on a beach. The words said "Full of natural fruit," but the drink was mostly sugar, so the ad was misleading. We also found ambiguity in the phrase "up to half off": only a few things were really that cheap. It is understandable that people believe ads, because they look so nice. By the end, we could discriminate between facts and opinions, and each of us wrote a short, coherent review of an ad. The lesson happened to coincide with a big sale in town, so we had plenty of examples.
items.passageZh: 上個月的媒體課，我們學會用批判的眼光看廣告。老師給我們看一則果汁飲料的廣告，畫面是一群光鮮亮麗的人在海灘上。廣告詞寫著「滿滿天然水果」，但那個飲料大部分是糖，所以這則廣告是在誤導人。我們也發現「最低半價」這句話有歧義：其實只有少數東西真的那麼便宜。人們會相信廣告是可以理解的，因為廣告看起來太美好了。課程結束時，我們已經能分辨事實和意見，每個人也都寫了一篇條理清楚的廣告短評。這堂課剛好碰上鎮上的大特賣，所以我們有很多例子可以用。

questions.questionZh: 為什麼說那則果汁廣告在誤導人？
為什麼這堂課有很多例子可以用？
options: 老師自己做了很多廣告
上課期間鎮上剛好有大型特賣

items.promptZh: 這隻狗能分辨不同車子的聲音。
referenceEn: This dog can discriminate between the sounds of different cars.
This dog is able to discriminate between different car sounds.
rubricZh: discriminate 的用法，例如 discriminate between 等
時態合理（例如 can discriminate、is able to 等）

items.promptZh: 每一道菜送出廚房前，這位主廚都會用挑剔的態度試吃。
referenceEn: The chef tastes every dish critically before it leaves the kitchen.
Before each dish leaves the kitchen, the chef tastes it critically.
rubricZh: critically 修飾動詞，表示「挑剔地」（例如 tastes … critically 等），位置不扣分
「送出廚房」可寫，例如 leaves the kitchen、is served 等；表示習慣（例如 tastes、will taste 等）
